decision: Comparison bars drawn to scale (linear) instead of log; narration and note say 'drawn to scale'.
rationale: On a log scale 28 vs 75,000 (or 40 vs 52,000) looked like a 1:3 difference, which hides the point of the episode. Linear shows the short trip as a glowing sliver, which is the true picture.
alternatives: Keep log scale with a note (rejected: viewers read bar length, not the note)

decision: Corrected the Voyager travel time: about 75,000 years at Voyager 1's 17.0 km/s (NASA), replacing 'over 89,000 years at more than 3 AU a year'. Hook now leads with 'Seventy-five thousand years.'
rationale: The old fact mis-stated 4.24 ly as ~63,000 AU (it is ~268,000 AU) and its wording ran backwards (a speed above 3 AU/yr gives under 89,000 years). The number is also the strongest hook in the episode; the old first line was a definition.
alternatives: Keep 3 AU/yr and say 'under 89,000' (rejected: NASA gives 17.0 km/s ≈ 3.6 AU/yr directly)

decision: Hook card shows 75,000 years (what the hook says) instead of 4.24 ly; Voyager card shows 17 km/s.
rationale: QA: the spoken hook and the card disagreed for the first 3 s; 4.24 ly is shown on the scale scene anyway.

decision: Proxima rebuilt around what can be seen: hook, Starshot and ship-clock are journey scenes (clocks to 75,000 yrs, 28 yrs, 10 min vs 4.24 yrs), the Voyager scene is the real Voyager 1 launch photo with speed chips.
rationale: Owner: 'I still miss visualisation… something to SEE, not only the numbers.' The episode was 5 number cards. No NASA-library image of Proxima itself exists (Hubble's Alpha Centauri A/B shows its companions, which would mislead under a Proxima label), so the star is drawn as a diagram body.
alternatives: Hubble Alpha Centauri A/B as the hook (rejected: not Proxima)
NASA artist concepts of Voyager (rejected: the launch photo is real)

decision: Destination photos as journey backdrops (NASA library, credited on screen)
rationale: Gives every trip a real place to arrive at; Proxima has no NASA photo, so Hubble's Alpha Centauri A and B is labelled as Proxima's neighbours
